title: openalex_W3016139316
universal_lens: Multiple-target tracking (MTT) integrates cognitive attention and computational memory; human MTT leverages neural resource allocation, while machine MTT employs bio-inspired optimization to emulate these behaviors. Multi-target tracking (MTT) algorithms integrate cognitive neuroscience insights, particularly attention and memory mechanisms, into computational frameworks mimicking human perception.
gsi_mapping: GSI models MTT via Bayesian belief propagation over spatiotemporal object tracks, incorporating conformal predictive uncertainty for robustness against adversarial motion patterns. GSI employs Bayesian inference to model uncertainty in MTT decisions, leveraging MOTA/MOTP metrics for probabilistic tracking accuracy and conformal prediction for robustness.
gse_mapping: GSE encodes MTT as a dynamic state-transition graph where each node represents a tracked target's pose and velocity, enabling real-time situational awareness through probabilistic reasoning. GSE utilizes state-transition models to simulate dynamic target behavior under occlusion and appearance variability, integrating memory-based LSTM modules for contextual awareness.

primitives.name: Cognitive Attention Allocation in MTT
primitives.verbatim_quote: Neuroscientists are interested in discovering the underlying neural mechanisms that successfully exploit cognitive resources, e.g., spatial attention or memory, during MTT.
primitives.assumptions: Human attention is limited and non-uniformly distributed across visual space; allocation follows a probabilistic model of saliency and task relevance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When number of targets exceeds cognitive capacity (~3-4), performance degrades due to attentional bottleneck.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian network models attention as a stochastic variable over object features; GSE uses attention-weighted Kalman filters for state estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Eye-tracking fixation density and reaction time variance

primitives.name: Bioinspired Optimization for MTT
primitives.verbatim_quote: Several past studies have examined how humans track targets simultaneously and what underlying behavioral and neural mechanisms they use.
primitives.assumptions: Biological systems optimize under constraints; algorithms mimic evolutionary or swarm-based strategies to approximate human behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When environmental complexity increases beyond algorithmic parameter tuning, convergence slows or fails.

layer2.mapping: GSE kernel incorporates particle swarm optimization (PSO) to simulate collective motion; GSI applies genetic algorithm (GA) to refine object trajectory predictions.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking accuracy vs. number of moving objects in synthetic video sequences

primitives.name: Human-Machine Complementarity in MTT
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper, we review MTT studies from both communities and discuss how findings from cognitive studies can inspire developers to construct higher performing MTT algorithms.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'Human performance index (dimensionless)', 'M': 'Machine performance index (dimensionless)', 'R': 'Relative improvement ratio (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Human cognition excels in ambiguous or novel contexts; machine learning excels in structured environments with sufficient training data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance divergence occurs when input variability exceeds training scope or when contextual novelty arises.

layer2.mapping: GSI fuses human-in-the-loop feedback into machine learning pipelines; GSE constructs hybrid decision trees combining expert rules with learned heuristics.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation error rates between human and algorithmic tracking under identical conditions

primitives.name: Neural Limitations in MTT
primitives.verbatim_quote: At the same time, computer-vision researchers have proposed different algorithms to track multiple targets automatically.
primitives.assumptions: Neurons exhibit bounded processing power; computational models must reflect these constraints to remain biologically plausible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When neural load exceeds threshold (L > C), tracking errors increase exponentially.

layer2.mapping: GSE simulates neuron-level resource depletion using dynamic programming; GSI applies entropy-based metrics to quantify cognitive overload.
layer2.telemetry: Neural activation maps from fMRI during MTT tasks compared to simulated algorithmic load profiles

primitives.breakdown_regime: When v_p approaches zero, the model reduces to pure serial processing.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian multi-object tracking filters where serial components handle identity association and parallel components handle spatial prediction.

primitives.name: Foveal vs Aqueous Information Allocation
primitives.verbatim_quote: When high-resolution information is needed for identifying a target, foveal vision is directed to it; on the other hand, when low-resolution information is sufficient for discriminating the targets, the eyes tend to land on blank areas to sample information from multiple targets covertly [22].

primitives.assumptions: Target discriminability depends linearly on allocated area, and total area is normalized (A_{foveal} + A_{aqueous} = 1).
primitives.breakdown_regime: As discriminability threshold approaches zero, A_{foveal} approaches 1 and A_{aqueous} approaches 0.

layer2.mapping: Conformal prediction regions in GSI where high-certainty targets receive focused attention (foveal) while uncertain targets receive distributed attention (aqueous).
layer2.telemetry: Average foveal allocation percentage and corresponding classification uncertainty metrics.

primitives.name: Processor Core Assignment for Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Leveraging the advantages of parallel programming, it is possible to recruit different cores of a processor and assign each core to track one target.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When C approaches infinity, the model predicts ideal linear speedup; practical limits arise from synchronization overhead.

primitives.name: Feature Discrimination in Visual Tracking

primitives.assumptions: Visual features must distinguish targets from background and other targets effectively.

primitives.name: Attention-Based Target Localization
primitives.verbatim_quote: MOTP shows the ability of an algorithm to determine the exact position of objects [92].
primitives.assumptions: Attention mechanisms enhance localization precision by focusing on salient regions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance drops during occlusion or high background clutter.

layer2.mapping: Attention pathways mirror visual stream processing, emphasizing spatial and temporal coherence in tracking.

primitives.name: Memory-Aware Tracking with LSTM
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the computer-vision domain, it is possible to extend such algorithms to track multiple objects, which is their rationale for inclusion in this section.
primitives.assumptions: Memory retention enables consistent identity maintenance across frames despite appearance variations.

primitives.name: Binocular Depth Enhancement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Human vision is binocular, and it has been reported that humans perform better when depth information is also available in MTT stimuli.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes human subjects utilize stereo disparity to discriminate overlapping trajectories in cluttered environments.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when stimuli are strictly 2D without parallax cues.

layer2.mapping: Maps binocular disparity to GSI conformal prediction intervals for 3D object trajectory forecasting, where the uncertainty ellipsoid captures depth ambiguity. Maps to GSE state-transition models via stereo visual odometry.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: Mean absolute error (MAE) reduction in predicted 3D bounding box locations when stereo input is enabled versus monocular baseline.

primitives.name: Spatial Configuration Utilization
primitives.verbatim_quote: However, there are still open questions about how and to what extent human binocular or even monocular depth vision influences the handling of challenges such as clutter, scale variance, and data association or occlusion.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes humans model target configurations as polygons or graphs, leveraging spatial relationships to resolve data association errors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when target configurations are highly dynamic and unpredictable.

layer2.mapping: Maps polygon vertex tracking to GSI particle filtering with configurational priors, reducing data association mistakes. Maps to GSE graph-based state estimation where nodes represent object centroids and edges represent spatial proximity.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: Optimal Subpattern Assignment (OSPA) distance improvement when configurational constraints are integrated into the tracker.

primitives.name: Semantic Grouping Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: Another problem faced by computer-vision–tracking algorithms is multiple-class MTT or tracking different objects from various categories, which is done easily by humans.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes humans employ semantic category-based grouping to prioritize attention and allocate tracking resources efficiently across heterogeneous object classes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when object categories share similar low-level features, causing misclassification.

layer2.mapping: Maps semantic grouping to GSI Bayesian multi-task learning frameworks, where shared latent factors encode common dynamics between classes. Maps to GSE federated tracking architectures that maintain separate hypothesis trees per object type.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: Average precision (AP) gain on cross-category tracking tasks when semantic priors are incorporated.

primitives.name: Parallel Processing Strategy
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is difficult for a computer-vision algorithm, especially one with a tracking-by-detection strategy, to manage this since these types of methods need one or more (pretrained) algorithms with the ability to detect different types of targets.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes humans exploit parallel processing pathways to simultaneously monitor distinct object trajectories regardless of class.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the number of targets exceeds approximately 4-5 concurrent tracks.

layer2.mapping: Maps parallel attentional tracking to GSI ensemble conformal predictors that run independent trackers in parallel and combine forecasts via weighted averaging. Maps to GSE hierarchical belief propagation where local trackers communicate global consistency constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Verification metric: Throughput improvement (tracks processed per second) and false negative rate reduction when parallel architecture is adopted.
